pr.title: fix(core): defer quiet-hours events instead of dropping them
pr.body:
<!-- git-stk:description -->
Closes #144.

Events suppressed by `rules.quiet_hours` were lost, not held. The filter dropped
them, the engine committed the source's snapshot anyway (only `DeliveryFailed`
scopes are held back), and since every source derives events by diffing against
that snapshot, they could never re-derive. A review request at 02:00 with a
23:00-08:00 window was silently discarded for good.

## What changed

`Decision` gains a `Defer(DeferReason)` variant, and quiet hours returns it
instead of `Drop`. `DropReason::QuietHours` is gone, since nothing produces it
any more.

The engine buffers deferred events in their own state-store bucket
(`__deferred__` / `pending`), alongside the existing digest buffer, and
`Engine::flush_deferred` releases them. The daemon calls it once per poll pass,
so an event surfaces within one interval of the window ending; `navi once` calls
it too, and reports how many it released.

Three details worth review:

- **Deferred events are re-decided on flush, not on the way in.** That is what
  makes per-repo `quiet_hours` overrides work without recording which window
  deferred what, and it means a mute or repo deny added overnight still applies
  on the way out. A buffered event whose rule now drops it is discarded.
- **Quiet hours is evaluated last in `decide`.** Anything another rule would drop
  is dropped, not parked, so the buffer only ever holds events the user wants.
- **A deferred event is marked delivered when buffered**, because the snapshot is
  about to advance past it. The buffer, not the snapshot, is what holds it from
  then on, so a delivery failure on release keeps it buffered for the next flush
  rather than discarding it.

`--dry-run` reports `WouldDefer` distinctly from `WouldDeliver`, and writes
nothing.

## Ordering against the digest

The digest check stays ahead of the defer check: a kind the user chose to batch
is already deferred by their own choice, and keeps the digest's cadence. The
digest flush itself still ignores quiet hours. That predates this change and is
left alone; worth a follow-up issue if you want the window to gate it.

## Tests

Six engine tests covering defer-then-release, the snapshot-advances regression
that motivated the issue, keep-on-delivery-failure, re-decide-on-flush, the
dry-run path, and drop-wins-over-defer. Assertions read the buffer contents
directly rather than trusting the flush's return count.

I mutation-tested the four load-bearing branches (discard instead of keep on
failure; release without re-deciding; deliver an event a rule now drops; never
buffer at all). All four are caught. The first pass of tests missed a fifth
mutant, which surfaced a real flaw: the buffer rewrite was gated on
`delivered > 0 || dropped > 0`, making `keep` dead when every release failed.
Correct by accident. It is now gated on `keep.len() != buffered`.

`just check` is clean: rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, markdownlint, full suite.
<!-- /git-stk:description -->

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #144
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: Held digest events are released only on the digest interval, so a mixed flush with a daily interval phased inside quiet hours strands the held events.

prior_bot.note: bot named the residual stranding case; author deferred it to a follow-up
